section_summary: This section contains U.S. State Department despatches, memoranda, letters, and reports from 1947 to 1949 concerning religious developments in occupied Japan. Major topics include Soviet efforts to dominate the Japanese Orthodox Church and SCAP's countermeasures, Catholic educational expansion and missionary activities, and travel clearance requests for Japanese Christian and Buddhist leaders. Additionally, the records document regional Asian concerns from Burma and India regarding American occupation policy, specifically protesting against the perceived favoring of Christian proselytization over Japan's Buddhist traditions.

subfiles.about: Reviews SCAP reports regarding Soviet attempts to exert control over the Japanese Orthodox Church and the denial of entry clearance to Soviet bishops.
subfiles.from: R. Davie, Division of Eastern European Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Reports on Soviet efforts to dominate the Japanese Orthodox Church by dispatching Soviet bishops, SCAP's denial of entry clearance, and the arrival of American Bishop Benjamin to assist the congregation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Soviet Attempts to Control the Japanese Orthodox Church

subfiles.about: Transmits an ozalid copy of Despatch No. 80 to Nanking regarding the acquisition of the Dairen Shinto Shrine by the Orthodox Church.
subfiles.from: H. Merrell Benninghoff, American Consul General, Dairen, China
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch transmitting to the Department of State a copy of Despatch No. 80 addressed to the Embassy in Nanking.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 77: Transmitting Copy of Despatch Entitled "Acquisition of Japanese Shinto Shrine by the Orthodox Church"

subfiles.about: Reports the transfer of the Dairen Shinto Shrine premises to the Russian Orthodox Church by Soviet occupation authorities.
subfiles.from: H. Merrell Benninghoff, American Consul General, Dairen, China
subfiles.summary: Reports that Soviet occupation authorities in Dairen transferred the former Japanese Dairen Shrine to the Orthodox Church via municipal proclamation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 80: Acquisition of Japanese Shinto Shrine by the Orthodox Church
subfiles.to: J. Leighton Stuart, American Ambassador, Nanking, China

subfiles.about: Designates an attached copy of Despatch No. 360 from Rangoon as the official record copy to replace the unreturned original.
subfiles.from: Division of Communications and Records (DC/R), Department of State
subfiles.summary: Replacement form designating an attached copy of Rangoon Despatch No. 360 as the official central record copy.
subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Form for Despatch No. 360 from Rangoon

subfiles.about: Transmits a Burmese newspaper editorial criticizing predictions that Japan will convert from Buddhism to Christianity.
subfiles.from: Earl L. Packer, American Consul General, Rangoon, Burma
subfiles.summary: Transmits an editorial from The Burman reacting to statements by Father Flanagan and arguing against replacing Buddhism with Christianity in Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 360: Editorialist Objects to Replacement of Japanese Buddhism by Christianity

subfiles.about: Inquires why Japanese Lutheran leader Chitose Kishi was prohibited by occupation authorities from attending an international conference in Sweden.
subfiles.from: Elsie Fuchs, Pauline Missionary Society of St. Mark's Lutheran Church, Evansville, Indiana
subfiles.summary: Inquires why occupation authorities barred Japanese Lutheran leader Chitose Kishi from attending the Lutheran World Federation meeting in Lund, Sweden.
subfiles.title: Letter from Elsie Fuchs Regarding Travel Clearance for Chitose Kishi
subfiles.to: The President of the United States, Washington, D.C.

subfiles.about: Explains policy restrictions on travel abroad by Japanese nationals in response to an inquiry about Chitose Kishi.
subfiles.from: Frank A. Schuler, Jr., Associate Chief, Division of Occupied Areas, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Explains Far Eastern Commission and SCAP policy restricting foreign travel by Japanese nationals, acknowledging the desire to restore cultural ties.
subfiles.title: Letter to Elsie Fuchs Regarding Travel Clearance for Chitose Kishi

subfiles.about: Reports U.S. Army G-2 intelligence findings regarding whether a Christian Front organization exists in Japan.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports Army intelligence findings that no direct evidence exists of a Christian Front in Japan, though Jesuit activities and Father Walsh are noted.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-16 Regarding Inquiries into a Christian Front in Japan

subfiles.about: Reports on the establishment of the Round Table Conference on Christian Culture and Peace and its discussions on democratization.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
keywords: Round Table Conference on Christian Culture and Peace
subfiles.summary: Reports on the formation of the Round Table Conference on Christian Culture and Peace under Teisaburo Sekiya, promoting religious education and democratic reorientation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 158: Round Table Conference on Christian Culture and Peace

subfiles.about: Records a conversation with Teisaburo Sekiya concerning Japanese attitudes toward students, labor unions, education, and the Occupation.
subfiles.from: Glen Bruner, Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Records Teisaburo Sekiya's views favoring education for former military students, criticizing labor agitation, urging foreign teacher recruitment, and supporting a prolonged Occupation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Attitudes of the Japanese Toward the Occupation; Hopes of the Japanese
subfiles.to: Files, Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits an English translation of a letter from Bishop Paul Y. Taguchi of Osaka concerning Catholic religious education in Japan.
subfiles.from: Frederic C. Behr, American Consulate General, Montreal, Canada
subfiles.summary: Transmits a translated letter from Bishop Paul Y. Taguchi of Osaka to a Canadian religious order regarding American teaching nuns.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 88: Religious Education in Japan

subfiles.about: Appeals for American Catholic teaching nuns to come to the Diocese of Osaka to establish schools under postwar religious freedom.
subfiles.from: Paul Y. Taguchi, Bishop of Osaka, Japan
subfiles.summary: Describes postwar religious freedom in Japan and appeals to a Canadian religious congregation to send American nuns to establish Catholic schools in Osaka.
subfiles.title: Translation of Letter from Bishop Paul Y. Taguchi to the Mother General of the Sisters of the Presentation of Mary
subfiles.to: Mother General, Congregation of Presentation of Mary, Saint-Hyacinthe, Quebec, Canada

subfiles.about: Transmits a copy of T. Mukoyama's request regarding Chief Abbot Kosho Otani's proposed visit to the United States for State Department reaction.
subfiles.from: Edgar Erskine Hume, Brigadier General, Chief, Reorientation Branch, Civil Affairs Division, Department of the Army
subfiles.summary: Transmits T. Mukoyama's letter regarding a proposed U.S. visit by Buddhist Chief Abbot Kosho Otani and requests State Department reactions.
subfiles.title: Letter from Brigadier General Edgar Erskine Hume to Dr. Daniel C. Buchanan Transmitting Request by T. Mukoyama
subfiles.to: Daniel C. Buchanan, Japanese-Korean Branch, Division of Occupied Areas, Department of State

subfiles.about: Requests permission for Chief Abbot Kosho Otani of Hompa Hongwanji to travel to the United States on a pastoral tour.
subfiles.from: T. Mukoyama, Hongwanji Buddhist Mission of North America
keywords: Hongwanji Buddhist Mission of North America
subfiles.summary: Requests travel permission for Chief Abbot Kosho Otani of Hompa Hongwanji to make a two- to three-month pastoral visit to American Buddhist congregations.
subfiles.title: Letter from T. Mukoyama Requesting U.S. Visit Clearance for Chief Abbot Kosho Otani
subfiles.to: Daniel Noce, Major General, Chief, Civil Affairs Division, Department of the Army

subfiles.about: States that Chief Abbot Kosho Otani's proposed travel does not fall within authorized categories and suggests referring the matter to SCAP.
subfiles.from: Frank A. Schuler, Jr., Chief, Japanese-Korean Branch, Division of Occupied Areas, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Advises that Abbot Kosho Otani's travel does not qualify under authorized travel categories and suggests referring the request to SCAP.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank A. Schuler, Jr. to Brigadier General Edgar E. Hume Regarding Kosho Otani
subfiles.to: Edgar Erskine Hume, Brigadier General, Chief, Reorientation Branch, Civil Affairs Division, Department of the Army

subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum from Hindu and Buddhist organizations in India objecting to Christian missionary proselytization in Japan.
subfiles.from: Howard Donovan, Counselor of Embassy, American Embassy, New Delhi, India
subfiles.summary: Transmits an Indian Hindu and Buddhist memorandum opposing Christian proselytization in Japan, advising that no official action is currently required.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 716: Transmission of Memorandum Objecting to Christian Missionary Activity in Japan

subfiles.about: Petitions the U.S. Government and General MacArthur to stop Christian missionary proselytization in Japan and void postwar conversions.
subfiles.from: J. Bhatt, Dharma Deva VidyaVachaspati, H. Saddhatissa, and associated Hindu and Buddhist organizations
subfiles.summary: Urges the United States Government and General MacArthur to halt Christian missionary proselytization in Japan, arguing Buddhism is the true barrier against communism.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Objecting to Christian Missionary Activity in Japan
